expectations.text: both-keys-declared-in-keys: {t}:leases and {t}:due are both passed in KEYS, not constructed inside the script body
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:47,93,94 use KEYS[1]/KEYS[2] only; no key name built in the script. DESIGN.md:23 `EVALSHA <sha> 2 {t}:leases {t}:due` and :31-36 shows the verified undeclared-key error at numkeys=0. Verified live on df-v1.34.0.

expectations.text: single-hmget-for-batch: the batch of up to 64 lease fields is read with one HMGET rather than per-item HGET
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:43-47 builds `fields` then `local stored = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], unpack(fields))`; the decision loop (56-89) issues no calls.

expectations.text: batched-hset-and-zadd-for-successes: successful renewals are written with one multi-field HSET and one multi-member ZADD (or equivalent single batched calls)
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:92-95 `if nh > 0 then redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], unpack(hset_args)); redis.call('ZADD', KEYS[2], unpack(zadd_args))`. Live 4-item run produced correct hash/zset state.

expectations.text: explicit-64-bound-and-chunking-awareness: the script enforces an explicit bound of 64 items and shows awareness of unpack/argument-count chunking limits
expectations.evidence: The 64 bound is enforced (renew_leases_batch.lua:16,26-29 MAX_ITEMS with rejection of n > 64), but there is no chunking/unpack-limit awareness anywhere: grep for 'unpack', 'chunk', 'stack' over DESIGN.md and transcript.md returns zero hits. DESIGN.md:138-140 only says peak memory is 'the <=128-element write argument lists'; it never notes the Lua unpack/argument-count ceiling or what to do if MAX_ITEMS is raised. Failure scenario: a later change to MAX_ITEMS=5000 hits a Lua stack overflow in `unpack(fields)` with no guidance in the design.

expectations.text: per-item-status-stable-protocol: the reply carries a per-item status covering renewed/token_mismatch/expired/missing with a stable constant-arity protocol
expectations.evidence: DESIGN.md:62-80 flat array of length 1+2N, `[2i]` status string 'renewed'|'token_mismatch'|'expired'|'missing', `[2i+1]` deadline or 0, request order, duplicates included. renew_leases_batch.lua:87-88 fills both slots on every path. Live: `1789529624032 renewed <dl> token_mismatch 0 expired 0 missing 0`.

expectations.text: server-time-used-for-deadline: the new deadline is computed from server time obtained on the server, per the stated contract
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:37-39 `local t = redis.call('TIME')` -> now_ms -> `new_deadline = now_ms + ttl_ms`; DESIGN.md:41-44 'The script takes no clock argument ... a client with a skewed clock cannot extend or kill a lease.'

expectations.text: measurement-plan-names-script-latency-and-equal-seed: the verification note names SCRIPT LATENCY or the eval coordination counters, an identical-seed comparison, and p50 plus p99
expectations.evidence: None of the three named elements is present. grep over DESIGN.md and transcript.md for 'script latency', 'coordination', 'p50', 'median' returns zero hits: the plan (DESIGN.md:158-244) uses redis-benchmark, INFO commandstats usec deltas, SLOWLOG and INFO latencystats only, and reports 'avg / p95 / p99' (:192), never p50. No identical-seed variant comparison either: DESIGN.md:186-190 drives `redis-benchmark -r 100000` with `m:__rand_int__`, i.e. randomized fields per arm, and section E (:225-228) compares against client pipelining without any equal-seed/identical-reply control.

expectations.text: no-unverified-redis-only-advice: the design contains no Redis-origin performance advice presented without Dragonfly evidence
expectations.evidence: Redis-cluster-origin placement claim stated as Dragonfly fact and never measured: DESIGN.md:13-14 'Both keys carry the same {t} hash tag, so Dragonfly maps them to **one shard**.' and :142-144 'The {t} hash tag keeps the transaction on one shard: Dragonfly takes locks on two keys in one shard instead of coordinating a multi-shard transaction.' On df-v1.34.0 defaults a hashtag is not the placement/lock unit (that requires --lock_on_hashtags), and the transcript shows no coordination-counter or flag check; yet the conclusion at :219-223 ('renew_leases_batch does not scale by adding shards or cores') is a shipping decision built on it. Also Redis 7 shebang syntax presented as the Dragonfly mechanism, unverified: :38-39 'Do **not** work around it with `#!lua flags=allow-undeclared-keys` - that flag makes the script run as a global transaction and removes the single-shard fast path' (Dragonfly's form is `--!df flags=`; the transcript never tests any flag). Plus unmeasured Redis lore at :174-175 'Always benchmark EVALSHA, never EVAL: EVAL re-parses and re-compiles and measures the compiler'.
